strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Binds active remote Mode Pack replacement and registry update admission to the exact approved, fetched candidate identity before active snapshot mutation.
Keeps candidate identity admission checks in the Rust runtime and fails closed before replacement, update admission, or approval consumption.
Carries bounded source and DNS binding evidence through approval, provenance, update admission, replacement, and replay without raw network or file content.
Lets unattended remote update flows prove they are activating the same fetched candidate that was approved and trusted.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime directly, with supporting progress for runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: modepack.replaceActive now requires exact approved/fetched candidate identity evidence for remote candidate activation and update admission, including source URL fingerprint, DNS resolution fingerprint, pinned address fingerprint, approval event, provenance, and trusted signer evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: R5.1 pins DNS during fetch, but replacement previously trusted only approval id, content hash, compiled policy, and partial update evidence; a stale cached candidate or replay path could not be checked against the full fetched identity tuple.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless registry update flows could fetch and approve a remote candidate, then activate a candidate whose source/DNS/provenance identity was not explicitly rebound at mutation time.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. R5.1 hardened network fetch execution; R5.2 hardens later active replacement and update admission using the fetched candidate identity.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing modepack.replaceActive path changes behavior; no method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. Existing approved candidate, provenance, and update admission summaries carry bounded evidence; no report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, or preview surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime fails before active snapshot replacement and before approval consumption when any expected approved candidate identity field mismatches current cached, approval, provenance, DNS, trust, or approval-event evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can safely decide whether to continue an autonomous remote update because mutation admission is tied to the exact candidate fetched, approved, and trusted earlier.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the second R5 trust-boundary step by carrying R5.1 fetch evidence into active mutation admission.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: R5.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and archives the R5.2 value gate. Review must confirm this is active remote Mode Pack mutation admission hardening, not an identity report wrapper.

exit_criteria: modepack.replaceActive requires approved remote candidate callers to provide exact candidate id, content hash, compiled policy fingerprint, source URL host/fingerprint, DNS binding fingerprints, and approval event id
active replacement fails before active snapshot mutation and before approval consumption when approved candidate identity evidence mismatches the cached fetched candidate or approval snapshot
registry update admission validates approved candidate provenance, trust, source URL, content, policy, and DNS binding evidence against the cached fetched candidate before mutation
consumed approval replay only succeeds for the same candidate activation and same approved/fetched identity evidence

successful replacement/update returns bounded identity evidence on existing result summaries without raw IPs, raw responses, raw Mode Pack JSON, raw registry manifests, prompts, provider responses, file content, command output, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, or secrets
no new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, or wrapper surface is added
